caption: Figure1: Overview of our approach, SCOPE, for conversation planning. During learning phase (left), we exploit dense semantic representation of conversations to learn a lightweight transition and reward model in semantic space (Notations and details covered in Sections 4.2 and 4.3). During runtime (right), SCOPE uses these learnt models to perform MCTS at a broader scope in semantic space without needing additional LLM queries for simulation (Algorithm 1), allowing us to select an optimal LLM response that maximizes the cumulative reward in a conversation.

Semantic space Conversation Planning with improved Efficiency (SCOPE) 1: Input: Initial conversation context s init . Transition model T and reward model R from learning phase (Sections 4.2 and 4.3). Pre-trained semantic embedding model f . k ≜ 0. Initial Qfunction Q k (s , ã ). Planning budget K. Branching factor m. Search depth D. 2: Propose m candidate LLM responses: {a 1 , a 2 , . . . , a m } . 3: Projection to semantic space: sinit ≜ f (s init ), ãj = f (s init + a j ) -f (s init ), ∀j = 1, 2, . . . , m 4: while k < K do 5: Select From root sinit , traverse search tree according to search policy π k (s) = arg max ã (Q k (s , ã) + U CT (s , ã)) until leaf state sleaf with unexplored action is reached. 6: At sleaf , pick a random unexplored action ãleaf . 7: Expand Conditioned on the selected action ãleaf , randomly sample a new state snew from learnt transition model T to simulate T (s leaf , ãleaf ) → snew .
